Probe P9/P10: independent create accepts what its add refuses. Grouped is unified but uses a weaker repository rule than the planner (P2), and no arm enforces the planner's inferred location at create (P3).

Grouped show and checkpoint share one classification on one state source; independent checkpoint uses a separate live-only classification. Stale-sensitive: the independent divergence is in item 05, which started from the baseline.

Independent reuses work checkpoint's ownership half and re-validates stored checkpoints; grouped shares only the Git rule and stores blank decisions. Stale-sensitive: the independent code is from the stale item 05.
Probes P4-P7 reproduce independent's mixed envelopes, rejection shapes and exit codes; survives excluding item 05.
Independent create/add/remove are unlocked (8 concurrent creates exit 0, 1 stored); grouped serializes all group writes (on its own lock, not work-protocol).
Baseline reuse favors independent (parser, executionLocation, event log; P2 shows the behavioral cost in grouped). Feature-internal shared helpers favor grouped (one parser, pipeline, renderer).
Two nested group-ID grammars in independent, applied to different domains; no contradictory behavior for stored groups. Introduced by stale item 05; does not survive the sensitivity analysis.
One file versus groups.json plus group-checkpoints.json for two separate concepts; membership provenance is not split in either arm. Organization only.
Probe P9/P10 reproduce M-D2. Grouped's unified rule is weaker than the planner's (P2 accepted in grouped, refused in independent), which the R2 evaluator missed.

Both arms' show and checkpoint disagree for abandoned and blocked members; grouped shares one view value but derives checkpoint lists inconsistently (abandoned members vanish), independent uses two sources but keeps abandoned explicit. Not evidence for either execution mode.
Independent requires active member and own execution, rejects blank decisions and validates checkpoint ownership; grouped does none. Not stale-sensitive in R2.

Grouped has one envelope and one coded rejection type; independent has one envelope family but uncoded string rejections with exit 1 for create/add/remove, coded ones for checkpoint, and a planner-style show with no JSON on not-found. The gap is clearly smaller than in A021.
Runtime probe confirms independent lost updates (8 exit 0, 1 stored); grouped serializes writes but reads lifecycle facts outside the lock.

Independent reuses executionLocation, the declaration reader and effectiveStatus; grouped re-derives location (P2) and terminal standing. Feature-internal helpers favor grouped (one pipeline, one codec).
Each arm has one group-ID grammar; the arms differ from each other (one vs two segments), which is not an intra-arm duplication.

category_definitions.divergent: More than one implementation, or one shared input derived differently, and concrete code or runtime evidence shows different behavior or invariants for the same input. Organization differences alone never qualify.
category_definitions.duplicated-compatible: More than one implementation or representation of the concern exists, but no CLI-reachable input produces contradictory behavior; the difference is organization, naming, file layout or message wording.
category_definitions.missing: The concern is not implemented where the items need it (for example no lock around a read-modify-write, or no ownership check).
category_definitions.not-assessable: The concern cannot be judged from the code at this commit (for example it requires an item that the sensitivity analysis excludes).
category_definitions.unified: One implementation (or one shared rule) serves every item that needs the concern, and every verb that exercises it shows the same behavior and invariant on the same input.
